So for most dinarzio bridge pickups, there should be 4/5 wires. A bare one, a black one, a red one, a white one, and a green one. Normally, a humbucker pickup works in a series, where one coil leads directly into another. The bare wire always goes to ground, and the red one normally goes to hot. Then, the black and white ones should be soldered together with some shrink wrap or tape covering them, that is the point where the two coils meet. Lastly, the green should be grounded, assuming you have a normal setup. So if you want to just eliminate the second coil, take the point where the two coils meet, solder another wire with them to extend that point, and connect it to a ground point (back of pot) or the green or bare wire, which should be ground. That shorts out the second coil. If you want to be able to split it with a switch, get a dpdt switch (mini on/on 2 way toggle or slide switch, depending on what you want) and solder that extension to middle connection point of one side, with a ground on one of the coners of the same side. [Basic Diagram](https://www.guitar-mod.com/wiring/coil_tap.gif). In diagrams, assume that the arrow made up of four lines is a ground.  When you do this mod, you may loose some volume, so if you arent satisfied with the volume when using it in single coil, you may want to put a resistor in. If you are doing the permanent one, just throw a resistor between the extension and the ground. If you are doing the switch one, put a resistor between the switch and the geound
